pages: The assessment of the internal network identified two critical findings, three high findings,
four medium findings and three low findings. The critical findings expose backups and
monitoring data to anyone on the staff network.
The client should fix the critical findings within seven days. The other findings fit the
normal maintenance cycle and are listed with a recommended owner.
Testing covered the server subnet, the VPN gateway and the domain controllers. The team
worked from a laptop on the staff network with a standard user account.
Scanning used the usual network scanner and a web proxy. Every automated result was
confirmed by hand before it entered this report.
The environment was in use during testing, so intrusive tests were avoided. Social engi
neering and physical access were out of scope.
Default credentials on the monitoring server
The monitoring server still accepts the vendor default administrator login. Anyone on the
staff network can sign in and read every host inventory record.

A share named backups allows anonymous read access. It holds database dumps that
include customer email addresses and hashed passwords.
Require authentication on the share and move the dumps to encrypted
Missing patch for remote code execution
The application server runs a library version with a public remote code execution exploit.
The vendor released a fix four months ago.
Apply the vendor update and add the host to the monthly patch cycle.
Cross-site scripting in the help desk form
The subject field of the help desk form is reflected without encoding. A crafted ticket runs
script in the browser of the agent who opens it.
Encode output in the ticket view and add a content security policy.
Figure 2: Evidence for finding 4: cross-site scripting in the help desk form
Session tokens stay valid for thirty days after the last use. A stolen token gives long lived
Expire idle sessions after fifteen minutes and rotate tokens at login.
Directory listing enabled on the build server
The build server lists the contents of its artifact directory to anyone who can reach it. The
listing shows internal project names and file versions.
Disable directory listing and require a login for the artifact area.

The two critical findings share a cause: services were deployed with their defaults and never
reviewed. A short checklist for new servers would have prevented both. The remaining
findings are routine and can be fixed with the patch cycle.
